reference: GNU coreutils tail is run independently by the harness in a reference Bash with its normal PATH. Expected byte output and statuses follow GNU/POSIX tail behavior; no candidate output is used to form expectations.
coverage: Default last-ten-line behavior on a regular file.
Line counts on a file whose final line lacks a newline.
Positive line counts on a pipe, using the streaming path.
Binary byte-tail output and positive byte offsets from stdin.
Repeated redirected stdin calls and use after a partial shell read.
GNU argument-error statuses for missing values, invalid values and unknown options.
Additional bounded edge cases and file effects are specified by the added parity cases.
exclusions: Follow append, truncation, retry, and rotation behavior is deferred because it needs a controlled asynchronous writer and bounded stop mechanism.
Locale-specific diagnostics, very large counts, and follow output ordering are not covered.

cases.purpose: Check GNU tail's default of the final ten lines on a seekable file containing twelve newline-terminated lines.
Check -n 2 when a regular file ends in a nonempty partial line without a final newline.
Check -n +2 on a pipe, which emits from the second line and exercises the non-seekable streaming path.
Check byte-exact handling of NUL and 0xff, for both the last four bytes and a positive byte offset on stdin.
cases.script:
printf '\000A\nB\377Z' > data
tail -c 4 data
tail -c +3 < data

cases.purpose: Check -z counts NUL-delimited records and preserves a final partial record without adding a delimiter.
Check default headers for multiple files and -q suppression across two invocations.
cases.script:
printf 'A\n' > first
printf 'B\n' > second
tail -n 1 first second
tail -q -n 1 first second

cases.purpose: Check that separate redirected stdin calls each read their input and that tail honors stdin's current offset after Bash read consumes one line.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
four
' > data
{ read -r first; tail -n 2; } < data
tail -n 1 < data
tail -n 1 < data

cases.purpose: Check GNU tail's nonzero status, empty stdout, and diagnostic presence for a missing relative fixture path.
Check status and diagnostic behavior for a malformed -n count; GNU coreutils tail reports an error with status 1.
Check Bash metadata identifies tail as a builtin and that its registered help documentation is available, without invoking an operational mode.
Exercise -f append delivery and -F pathname retry/rotation behavior under a controlled writer.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM fixture with a supervised asynchronous writer that appends to a relative file, renames and recreates it for -F, and stops the tail process through a private bounded supervisor. The one-shot comparison fixture cannot reliably schedule inotify events or verify follow lifecycle and clean shutdown.
